hypothesis.text: Arkansas can redesign education from early childhood through lifelong advanced learning as an integrated human-capital, economic-development, civic-development, and public-wealth system that converts inherited natural, institutional, intellectual, and financial capital into greater human capability—giving every bona fide resident child a world-class developmental foundation while strategically building, retaining, and practicing the capabilities Arkansas needs—through bona fide residency and public-investment rates (not citizenship tests), premium nonresident access that can feed Human-Capital External Income, a positive residency-and-service compact, an Arkansas Learning Network, regional centers of excellence, public-contribution-proportionate research upside, and permanent adult reskilling—without exit penalties, without calling the system 'free,' and within constitutional travel and residency constraints.
hypothesis.central_question: Can Arkansas redesign education from early childhood through lifelong advanced learning as an integrated human-capital, economic-development, civic-development, and public-wealth system that gives every child a world-class foundation while strategically building and retaining the capabilities Arkansas needs?
hypothesis.conceptual_spine: Education is the process by which Arkansas converts its inherited natural, institutional, intellectual and financial capital into greater human capability—and every generation is expected to leave the state's stock of capability and prosperity larger than it found it.
hypothesis.design_posture: Arkansas should treat education as a public capital investment in human capability—not as an unlimited transferable benefit with no expectation of contribution back to the state. Frame rates and access around bona fide Arkansas residency and Arkansas public investment, not Arkansas citizenship.
hypothesis.long_term_vision: Arkansas becomes a learning society in which every stage of education deliberately builds the health, knowledge, skills, ownership, civic capacity, and productive power of its people—and every critical capability Arkansas needs can ultimately be learned, practiced, and built inside Arkansas.
hypothesis.desired_end_state_formulation: Arkansas invests heavily in Arkansans, sells world-class educational capacity to the rest of the world, recruits the people it wants to become Arkansans, and keeps a durable share of the economic value its public institutions help create.

governance.reason: Registered under CC-DEC-138; operating architecture locked under CC-DEC-139; Intergenerational Arkansas Capital research layer locked under CC-DEC-144. Not a new principle. Not a fifth empirical pass. Four operating passes remain in order. Parallel until Demand Map build. Main fiscal evidence lane unchanged (food-hub / External Income).

forbidden: arkansas citizenship for tuition or education rates
our intellectual property belongs to the people as literal state ownership of every idea
language_lock.why: Teachers, clinicians, buildings, and laboratories cost real labor and capital; taxpayers and businesses finance them. 'Free' erases the investment compact. 'Citizenship' is the wrong legal and philosophical frame for education rates — use bona fide residency and public investment.

economic_bargain.statement: Arkansas will invest more deeply in your potential than almost anywhere in America. In return, we expect you to use that capability to build a productive life, contribute to your community, and strengthen the society investing in you.

intergenerational_arkansas_capital.core_idea: Arkansas taxpayers, families, institutions, land, research, infrastructure, and generations of accumulated public investment have built educational assets. Bona fide Arkansas residents should receive the strongest public investment rate; nonresidents should pay a premium that reflects the real value of access to those assets.
intergenerational_arkansas_capital.inheritance_obligation: Every generation receives an Arkansas inheritance. Its responsibility is not merely to consume it, but to enlarge it and pass a stronger inheritance to the next generation.

capital_categories.natural_capital: land, water, minerals, forests, agricultural productivity
capital_categories.physical_capital: roads, universities, laboratories, hospitals, utilities, public buildings
capital_categories.human_capital: generations of teachers, scientists, workers, farmers, engineers, physicians, entrepreneurs
capital_categories.institutional_capital: legal systems, universities, extension services, research institutions, public datasets
capital_categories.intellectual_capital: publicly financed research, plant science, medical research, software, technology, patents and accumulated knowledge

intergenerational_arkansas_capital.transaction_model: Arkansas creates exceptional value → outsiders voluntarily pay for access to that value → part of that money permanently strengthens Arkansas.

flow_redirection.desired: Arkansas resources → Arkansas education → Arkansas capability → Arkansas innovation → Arkansas ownership → Arkansas wealth → reinvestment in Arkansans
flow_redirection.rejected_status_quo_pattern: Arkansas resources → outside processing / outside ownership / graduate leaves → wealth exits Arkansas
flow_redirection.implication: Education overhaul is not merely school reform — it is one mechanism for changing the direction of the flow

linked_hypotheses.HYP-130: Capability need map — what Arkansas must build and practice
linked_hypotheses.HYP-131: Human-Capital External Income + public IP/royalty paths feed Replacement Stack only when reserved cash is real
linked_hypotheses.HYP-132: Residency rules prevent benefit tourism, not talent immigration; strategic recruits may be invested in to become Arkansans

stage_1_birth_through_grade_12.name: Universal human-capital foundation
stage_1_birth_through_grade_12.rule: Publicly guaranteed for bona fide resident children. No tuition concept. This is the universal human-capital foundation.
stage_1_birth_through_grade_12.guarantee: Arkansas guarantees every bona fide resident child access to the developmental foundation needed to become an independent adult and contributor to shared prosperity.
stage_1_birth_through_grade_12.health_rationale: A child cannot learn well if their teeth hurt, they cannot see the board, or their family cannot reach a physician.

stage_2_ages_14_18.name: Pathway formation
stage_2_ages_14_18.rule: Increasingly personalized; not pigeonholing; stop treating a bachelor's degree as the only prestigious destination.
stage_2_ages_14_18.cte_posture: Build CTE into the main spine of education rather than a side program; Arkansas already has substantial statutory CTE / concurrent-education infrastructure.

students_as_builders.rule: Change the distinction between school and economy — supervised real systems, not only classroom study.

stage_3_advanced_education.name: Arkansas capacity investment
stage_3_advanced_education.rule: Higher, graduate, professional, and heavily subsidized specialty programs increasingly tied to state strategic need — and priced by bona fide residency / public investment, not citizenship.

access_and_pricing_tiers.arkansas_resident: Deeply publicly invested Arkansas Resident Investment Rate after a defensible residency / domicile test
access_and_pricing_tiers.new_bona_fide_resident: Qualifies after legitimate residency criteria — person must be allowed to prove bona fide residence; no permanent nonresident label merely because they moved recently (Vlandis v. Kline, 412 U.S. 441)
access_and_pricing_tiers.nonresident: Premium market rate reflecting value of scarce elite seats — not merely cost-plus — optimized for Arkansas public return without undermining quality, enrollment, research reputation, talent recruitment, or federal constraints
access_and_pricing_tiers.strategic_recruit: Scholarships / investment when Arkansas deliberately wants that person to become an Arkansan — prevent benefit tourism, not talent immigration (HYP-132)

human_capital_external_income.concept: Nonresident and international premium tuition on world-class Arkansas educational capacity can import outside dollars — a Human-Capital External Income stream for HYP-131
human_capital_external_income.illustrative_not_counted: e.g. thousands of premium-paying students from neighboring states or overseas
human_capital_external_income.count_rule: Illustrative enrollment × premium is not COUNTABLE until reserved cash and incidence are bound
human_capital_external_income.optimization_question: What nonresident price maximizes Arkansas public return without undermining program quality, enrollment, research reputation, talent recruitment, or federal constraints?

strategic_human_capital_demand_map.chain: Need → available seats → graduates → shortages → geographic shortage → program expansion required

stage_4_adult_lifelong.name: Permanent adult education
stage_4_adult_lifelong.rule: Accessible continuous reskilling — not unlimited taxpayer-paid degrees.
stage_4_adult_lifelong.ai_era_path: worker → displaced by automation → short credential → apprenticeship → new occupation
stage_4_adult_lifelong.employer_role: Employers in Workforce Prosperity help finance reskilling

workforce_transition_plan.trigger: Automation materially displaces employees at firms receiving public incentives or participating in prosperity system
workforce_transition_plan.goal: Automation increases prosperity without abandoning workers whose productivity helped build the company

residency_and_service_compact.name: Positive residency-and-service compact
residency_and_service_compact.rejected_design: You received an Arkansas education, therefore you may not leave
residency_and_service_compact.rejected_why: Runs into constitutional rights of travel and related federal protections; qualitatively different from bona fide residency for tuition rates

legal_room_research_posture.state_practice: Arkansas public institutions already distinguish residents from nonresidents; bona fide domicile and continuous residence used for in-state reclassification (e.g. University of Arkansas practices — research to bind primary rules).
legal_room_research_posture.federal_posture: States may distinguish residents from nonresidents for public-university tuition. Vlandis v. Kline, 412 U.S. 441 (1973): reasonable durational residency requirements may protect preferential rates for bona fide residents and deter moving in solely for subsidized tuition, but the person must be allowed to prove bona fide residence — permanent/irrebuttable nonresident labels based solely on prior out-of-state address are out.
legal_room_research_posture.implication: Legal room to favor genuine residents exists; exit walls and citizenship tests do not; benefit-tourism prevention must not become talent-immigration prevention.

three_separate_legal_tests.rule: Do not blend these into one vague 'can we make college free for Arkansans?' memo

tests.question: How strong can bona fide residency requirements for subsidized higher education legally be?
How much premium can Arkansas lawfully and economically charge nonresidents?
How can Arkansas capture a continuing public return from publicly financed research and advanced educational assets without undermining academic freedom, private innovation, or talent attraction?

arkansas_resident_investment_rate.rule: Available only after genuine Arkansas residency / domicile or Arkansas K–12 history (and other constitutionally valid categories) — after a defensible residency test showing Arkansas is actually home, not merely the location of a university
arkansas_resident_investment_rate.note: Arkansas already uses residency concepts for state-funded scholarships — bind current rules before inventing new tiers.

state_strategic_capacity_contract.applies_to: Programs Arkansas heavily subsidizes because the state urgently needs the profession

structure.public_provides: Substantial tuition assistance or education financing
recipient_chooses: Serve/invest in Arkansas for X years
OR repay a defined portion of the additional public subsidy

state_strategic_capacity_contract.analogy: Service-obligation scholarship models — investment contract, not exit tax
state_strategic_capacity_contract.illustrative_not_locked: We will invest $80,000 in your specialty education if you help provide the capability Arkansas needs — including strategic recruits Arkansas wants to become Arkansans
state_strategic_capacity_contract.departure: Leave without service → repay contractual subsidy
state_strategic_capacity_contract.incentive_framing: Stay because Arkansas invested in you and offers an attractive professional life here
state_strategic_capacity_contract.hyp132_join: Residency rules prevent benefit tourism, not talent immigration

public_research_ip_ownership.rule: If Arkansas finances research that produces valuable crop technology, medical discovery, AI systems, or industrial processes, the citizens' investment should be visible in commercialization — without claiming literal state ownership of every idea created in Arkansas.
public_research_ip_ownership.better_formulation: The public's claim should correspond to the public contribution — not 'our intellectual property belongs to the people' as blanket state ownership of every idea.
public_research_ip_ownership.chain: research → IP → license/equity/royalty → university reinvestment + researcher reward + public prosperity return
public_research_ip_ownership.implication: Education becomes a public-income asset, not only an expenditure

arkansas_learning_network.rule: Education should be a statewide network, not dozens of competing silos that independently duplicate everything.
arkansas_learning_network.hyp130_anchor: HYP-130 inventory found 1,759 strategic programs across Arkansas higher education — specialization and join, not universal duplication.
arkansas_learning_network.implication: Institutional geography stops determining educational opportunity

regional_centers_of_excellence.rule: Deliberately place advanced educational capabilities across Arkansas — not everything to Fayetteville or Little Rock.
illustrative_centers_not_locked: North Central Food Systems & Regenerative Agriculture Center

legal_gate_taxonomy.rule: Each track and major design element must be classified before scale claims.
legal_gate_taxonomy.purpose: Build honest 8–16 year transition without inventing legal clearance

linked_hypotheses.HYP-124: Distributed Prosperity Network — regional centers and access standard
linked_hypotheses.HYP-129: Arkansas transition pathway — Layer-1 programs — where we prove it locally
linked_hypotheses.HYP-130: Strategic Capacity Audit — what capability Arkansas needs; 1,759-program inventory
linked_hypotheses.HYP-131: Public-income engines — Human-Capital External Income + public IP/royalty paths when reserved cash is real
linked_hypotheses.HYP-132: Population-Wealth Attraction — prevent benefit tourism, not talent immigration; strategic recruits

system_chain.statement: HYP-130 tells Arkansas what capability it needs. HYP-133 builds the people capable of doing it — converting intergenerational Arkansas capital into greater human capability. HYP-129 determines where we prove it locally. HYP-132 gives those people reasons to stay, return, raise families and build wealth here. HYP-131 captures enough resulting prosperity (including Human-Capital External Income and public-contribution IP returns) to reduce compulsory taxation.
system_chain.implication: Coherent system — not separate policy proposals

conceptual_layer_lock.name: Intergenerational Arkansas Capital research layer
conceptual_layer_lock.rule: Spine deepen allowed; does not add a fifth empirical pass or reopen conceptual branching. Pass order unchanged.

operating_architecture_passes.posture: Stop adding conceptual branches; prove operating architecture in this order when HYP-133 gets its next substantial pass

passes.name: Residency-and-Service Compact legal design
passes.deliverable: Serious constitutional/legal memo before policy — three separate legal tests
passes.hard_rule: Repayment tracks the incremental public subsidy — not punitive tuition debt or exit tax. Frame residency/public investment, not citizenship.

passes.name: Arkansas Learning Network + Centers of Excellence
questions: What capability simply does not exist in Arkansas?
passes.rule: When something important is absent, generate a specific BUILD/EXPAND/PARTNER/IMPORT-TEMPORARILY recommendation — do not merely record a gap

passes.name: Full implementation/legal matrix
passes.deliverable: 8–16 year Arkansas implementation program — not an education manifesto
